skill.name: The Eye of the United Dragon
skill.trigger: Effect 1 happens once at the start of the duel (nothing for you to do). Effects 2 and 3 can each be used once per duel, and only if your deck holds 15 or more Dark Magician cards and cards that mention it.
skill.enabler: Effect 2 needs Timaeus the United Dragon in your hand: shuffle 1 other card from your hand into your deck, Timaeus is played from your hand, and you add 2 Dark Magician cards. Illusion of Chaos and Preparation of Rites (which searches Illusion of Chaos) are ways to get Timaeus. Effect 3 needs you to control "Dark Magician" or your opponent to control a monster: it plays Dark Magician or Dark Magician Girl from your deck face-down and gives you The Eye of Timaeus.

adds.note: Added to your hand from outside your deck when you use effect 3.

dark-magician.gamePlan: Everything starts from Timaeus the United Dragon: if you hold it (or Illusion of Chaos or Preparation of Rites to fetch it) the skill turns the hand into a full combo, which the creator calls a one-card combo. Play Magician's Rod, use Illusion Magic to bring Dark Magician cards to your hand, fuse the Dragon Knight, use the skill's second effect for The Dark Magicians, and keep the extra cards for later. You finish with a monster that negates, one that flips opposing monsters face-down, two Magician Navigations in the Graveyard that negate Spells and Traps, and The Gaze of Timaeus ready to bring Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon in on the opponent's turn. If you miss Dark Magical Curtain, play extra Magician's Rod and Preparation of Rites; with only one Curtain you are still fine, because the combo searches it.
strengths: A one-card combo: with Timaeus (or a way to get it) in hand the skill builds the rest.
Soul Servant, Dark Magical Circle and Illusion of Chaos let you put cards back in your deck, so the combo is hard to brick.
It ends with several negates and a monster that resists the opponent's effects, and the creator rates it as good enough for King of Games.
weaknesses: Hand traps (D.D. Crow on the Graveyard, Droll & Lock Bird) can cut parts of the combo; keep a second Soul Servant as a safety net.
The order matters: the Dragon Knight goes in a main Monster Zone and The Dark Magicians in the Extra Monster Zone.
It is based on one creator's video and his own replays, and the opponents' answers in the replays vary.

scenarios.title: Turn 1: with Timaeus (or Illusion of Chaos) in your hand, build the full negate board

anyOf.label: Timaeus the United Dragon, or a way to fetch it (Illusion of Chaos or Preparation of Rites)

skillPlan.note: Uses effect 2 right away (it plays Timaeus) and effect 3 once Dragon Knight is on the field.

start.note: The creator's starting hand. Yours will differ: any hand that gets Timaeus into your hand works, and without Magician's Rod the skill adds Rod and Illusion Magic instead.

steps.reason: Reveal Illusion of Chaos from your hand (it stays in your hand) to add Timaeus the United Dragon from your deck, then put 1 card from your hand on top of your deck. Put away a card you do not need for this line (here, Magician Navigation). Illusion of Chaos is only the way to get Timaeus: any other way to get it into your hand works too.

steps.skill: The Eye of the United Dragon
steps.when: Right after you have Timaeus the United Dragon in your hand
steps.needs: Timaeus the United Dragon in your hand, and 1 card from your hand to shuffle into your deck (the creator shuffles Dark Magician Girl).
steps.gives: Timaeus is played from your hand for free, and you add 2 cards that are Dark Magician or mention it. With Magician's Rod already in your hand, take Illusion Magic and Soul Servant; without Rod, take Rod and Illusion Magic.
steps.reason: This is the skill's effect 2, the heart of the deck: it puts Timaeus on the field without spending your Normal Summon and finds the next two combo cards.
Normal Summon Magician's Rod and search a Spell/Trap that names Dark Magician. The creator takes a second Soul Servant, because he wants one to discard to Summoner Monk later.
Tribute Magician's Rod (a Spellcaster) to add 2 copies of Dark Magician from your deck to your hand.

Use Timaeus's effect to Fusion Summon Dark Magician the Dragon Knight: Dark Magician from your hand plus Timaeus (a Dragon) as the materials. Put the Dragon Knight in a MAIN Monster Zone, not the Extra Monster Zone: the next steps need the Extra Monster Zone free. The Dragon Knight is treated as Dark Magician, which turns on the skill's effect 3, and it protects your Spells and Traps from the opponent's effects.

steps.skill: The Eye of the United Dragon
steps.when: Once you control Dark Magician the Dragon Knight (it counts as Dark Magician)
steps.needs: A "Dark Magician" on your side of the field (the Dragon Knight counts).
steps.gives: Play Dark Magician Girl from your deck face-down, and add The Eye of Timaeus to your hand from outside your deck.
steps.reason: This is the skill's effect 3: it gives you Dark Magician Girl as fusion material and a free fusion Spell, both without using up any cards from your hand.

Use The Eye of Timaeus on the face-down Dark Magician Girl to Fusion Summon The Dark Magicians. Put it in the EXTRA Monster Zone (the creator stresses this): that is where it waits before it becomes the Xyz monster later.

Activate Soul Servant to put Magician Navigation (a Dark Magician card) on top of your deck. Because you activated a Spell, The Dark Magicians can draw 1 card, and it draws that Navigation. A Trap you draw this way can be activated the same turn. In the replay the opponent banished this Soul Servant from the Graveyard with D.D. Crow, which does not matter because you hold a second copy.

Activate Magician Navigation: Special Summon Dark Magician from your hand, then Special Summon Summoner Monk (a Level 4 DARK Spellcaster) from your deck. Navigation will sit in your Graveyard to negate a Spell or Trap on the opponent's turn.

You have activated a Spell/Trap this turn, so you can Special Summon Dark Magician of Destruction from your Extra Deck by banishing a Level 6 or higher DARK Spellcaster you control (the Dark Magician). Its search adds Dark Magical Curtain.

Dark Magician of Destruction and The Dark Magicians are both Level 8, so Xyz Summon Number 90: Galaxy-Eyes Photon Lord with them. It will negate a monster effect on the opponent's turn and it takes The Dark Magicians' place in the Extra Monster Zone.
Summoner Monk discards a Spell (the spare Soul Servant) to Special Summon a Level 4 monster from your deck: take Chronicle Sorceress. The summoned monster cannot attack, which does not matter here.

Dark Magician is in your Graveyard and it is DARK, so Chronicle Sorceress can send 1 Dark Magician card from your deck to the Graveyard. Send the second Magician Navigation: it is a second Spell/Trap negate waiting for the opponent's turn.

Summoner Monk and Chronicle Sorceress are two Level 4 DARK monsters, so Xyz Summon Evilswarm Nightmare. It can flip a monster the opponent Special Summons face-down. This is the creator's favourite, but the two Level 4 monsters can become any other Level 4 DARK Xyz or Link monster you prefer.

Activate Dark Magical Curtain: you Special Summon a Dark Magician from your deck (the opponent also gets to Special Summon a DARK Spellcaster, and neither side can use those monsters' effects this turn). Because it is a real Dark Magician you add a Spell/Trap that mentions it: The Gaze of Timaeus.

Banish the Soul Servant in your Graveyard to draw cards equal to the number of different Dark Magician and Dark Magician Girl cards on the field and in the Graveyards (here 2: Dark Magician and Dark Magician Girl). Your deck is thin by now, so you are likely to draw useful cards.

The creator happened to draw Magician's Salvation; activating it also Sets Eternal Soul directly from your deck. Eternal Soul makes your Dark Magicians unaffected by the opponent's card effects once it is face-up. This step depends on your draws: with other cards, this part is your own choice.

Set The Gaze of Timaeus. During the opponent's turn it Fusion Summons Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon (using the Dark Magician on your field), which negates one more activation. The creator sums up the finished turn: 1 monster effect negate, 2 face-down flips, 2 Spell/Trap negates and 1 negate of anything.

scenarios.chainNotes: Chain the Rod search and the other searches in response to anything the opponent plays, so a hand trap cannot cancel the rest. Keep Magician Navigation in the Graveyard for the opponent's turn: it banishes itself to negate a Spell/Trap. Put the Dragon Knight in a main Monster Zone and The Dark Magicians in the Extra Monster Zone.
scenarios.endBoard: Number 90: Galaxy-Eyes Photon Lord (negates a monster effect), Evilswarm Nightmare (flips Special Summoned monsters face-down), Dark Magician the Dragon Knight (protects your Spells/Traps) and a Dark Magician, with Eternal Soul and The Gaze of Timaeus set and two Magician Navigations in the Graveyard (two Spell/Trap negates). The Gaze brings Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon on the opponent's turn for one more negate.
scenarios.weakSpots: D.D. Crow can banish a Soul Servant from the Graveyard (keep a second one); Droll & Lock Bird stops searches and draws, so chain them early; if the opponent removes the Dark Magician on your field, The Gaze and Eternal Soul get weaker. The creator says that going second the skill's effect 3 gives you a free Dark Magician or Dark Magician Girl and the combo changes.

scenarios.title: Going second: use the skill to get Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon out first, then build the Dragon Knight

skillPlan.note: Uses effect 3 first (free Dark Magician and The Eye of Timaeus), then effect 2 for Timaeus, Magician's Rod and Illusion Magic.

start.note: The creator's hand in his first going-second replay: three Dark Magical Curtains, Timaeus the United Dragon and Photon Jumper. Yours will differ: the line works with any hand that keeps Timaeus, and the opponent's plays decide what you can finish.

steps.skill: The Eye of the United Dragon
steps.when: First thing in your turn, as soon as the opponent controls a monster (going second, this is almost always true)
steps.needs: Your opponent controls a monster (or you control a "Dark Magician").
steps.gives: Play 1 Dark Magician from your deck, and add The Eye of Timaeus to your hand from outside your deck.
steps.reason: This is the skill's effect 3, used first when you go second: it gives you a Dark Magician on the field and The Eye of Timaeus for free, so you can bring out Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon before the opponent's turn comes.

Use The Eye of Timaeus on the Dark Magician to Fusion Summon Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon (the Eye counts as a Dragon here). Dragoon cannot be destroyed or targeted by effects, can destroy an opponent's monster, and can negate one activation (it discards 1 card). The creator wants it out first because the opponent can use hand traps or draw effects against the rest of the turn. The Extra Monster Zone is a good place for it.

steps.skill: The Eye of the United Dragon
steps.when: Right after Dragoon is out, while you still hold Timaeus the United Dragon
steps.needs: Timaeus the United Dragon in your hand, and 1 card from your hand to shuffle into your deck (a spare Dark Magical Curtain here).
steps.gives: Timaeus is played from your hand, and you add Magician's Rod and Illusion Magic to your hand.
steps.reason: This is the skill's effect 2. With three Curtains in the starting hand, shuffling one back costs you nothing.
Normal Summon Magician's Rod and search a Spell/Trap that names Dark Magician: Soul Servant.
Tribute Magician's Rod (a Spellcaster) to add 2 copies of Dark Magician from your deck to your hand.

Activate Soul Servant to put Dark Magical Circle on top of your deck, then banish Soul Servant from the Graveyard right away to draw 1 card (the number of different Dark Magician cards on the field and in the Graveyards: here just Dark Magician). You draw the Circle.

Activate Dark Magical Circle: look at the top 3 cards of your deck and add a Dark Magician card or a Spell/Trap that mentions it; the creator finds Eternal Soul. Each time a Dark Magician is summoned the Circle can banish a card the opponent controls.

Use Timaeus's effect again: Fusion Summon Dark Magician the Dragon Knight from a Dark Magician in your hand and Timaeus. It counts as a Dark Magician, so the Circle triggers and banishes an opponent's card (the creator banished a Pentest here; pick the card that hurts you most). It also protects your Spells and Traps.

Set Eternal Soul. Once it is face-up, your Dark Magicians are unaffected by the opponent's card effects, and on the opponent's turn it can bring a Dark Magician back from your hand or Graveyard. Keep the other Dark Magician and the spare Curtains in your hand for the next turn.

scenarios.chainNotes: Bring Dragoon out first and keep it for the opponent's turn: it is the card that negates what the opponent does next. In the replay the opponent used D.D. Crow, Mascarena and a draw effect during the turn, and the creator used Dragoon to negate the draw.
scenarios.endBoard: Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon and Dark Magician the Dragon Knight on the field, Dark Magical Circle face-up and Eternal Soul set, with a Dark Magician and two Dark Magical Curtains still in your hand for the next turn.
scenarios.weakSpots: The opponent can answer Dragoon with a hand trap or a board wipe, and the steps after step 2 depend on what the opponent does; the creator himself made mistakes in this game (banishing the wrong card with the Circle). Treat this as a model of what to aim for, not as a line you can always finish.

skill.name: Precious Cards of the Dark
skill.trigger: Needs 6 or more DARK monsters in your deck: Imsety x3 and D.D. Crow x3 are exactly 6, so do not swap a D.D. Crow for a card that is not DARK. You can use it once per turn and twice per duel.
skill.enabler: No special card is needed. During your Main Phase put 1 card from your hand on the bottom of your deck or send it to the Graveyard, then draw 2 cards (3 if it is the first turn of the player going second). The deck has no way to search, so the skill is what gives it consistency.

sideSkills.name: Precious Cards of the Wind
sideSkills.reason: The creator says you can also use the Wind version: Hapi, 2 Mulcharmy Fuwalos and 3 Droll & Lock Bird are 6 WIND monsters. He picked the Dark one because not everyone owns the Wind cards. There is also a version with Galaxy Photon that he found more annoying.

sideSkills.name: Precious Cards of the Light
sideSkills.reason: The creator says you can also use the Light version of the skill. It needs 6 LIGHT monsters in the deck, which this list does not have, so you would have to change the deck. The Galaxy Photon version, which mixes in LIGHT cards, is the one he found more annoying and did not want to play.

sources.title: Curso completo de Horus (Portuguese deck course and replays)
sources.creator: Sorem

horus.gamePlan: Horus is a very simple, bread-and-butter deck for the beginner: you play Spells that send your Horus monsters to the Graveyard, and they come back on their own while you control King's Sarcophagus. Start with Imsety, Walls of the Imperial Tomb or King's Sarcophagus, fill the field with Level 8 monsters, make Coach King Giantrainer (draw cards), then I:P Masquerena, and keep a Set Canopic Protector so you can bring a monster back and Link Summon on the opponent's turn. Each Horus monster also does something when the opponent removes one of your cards, so baiting their interaction is the plan. About half of the main deck is staples (hand traps and Kaijus), and the Extra Deck is the expensive part.
strengths: It is easy to play: the line is nearly the same every time and does not have long branches.
Your Horus monsters are protected from effects that do not target them and come back from the Graveyard, so it is hard to stop with one interruption.
Canopic Protector gives you plays on the opponent's turn, and the deck draws a lot of cards.
It is very strong in the current ranked meta and reaches King of Games easily.
weaknesses: Only 9 real starters, so hands without Imsety, Walls or King's Sarcophagus brick.
Spell and Trap removal (Cosmic Cyclone, Mystical Space Typhoon) hits King's Sarcophagus and Canopic Protector, which are continuous cards that fail if destroyed while activating.
The Extra Deck is expensive: several Rank 8s, I:P Masquerena and S:P Little Knight come from bundles or are hard to get.
Horus the Black Flame Deity is hard to time: the opponent must remove one of your cards first, and it clears your own field.

cards.name: Imsety, Glory of Horus
cards.note: The main starter. From the Graveyard it Special Summons itself while you control King's Sarcophagus. Discard it and 1 more card from your hand to add King's Sarcophagus from the deck and draw 1. When the opponent removes one of your cards it sends a card from the field to the Graveyard without targeting.

cards.name: King's Sarcophagus
cards.note: The most important card of the deck. Your Horus monsters cannot be destroyed by effects that do not target them. Send 1 card from your hand to send a Horus monster from your deck to the Graveyard (up to 4 times per turn), and once per turn a Horus monster that battles can send the opponent's monster to the Graveyard.

cards.name: Walls of the Imperial Tomb
cards.note: Field Spell that counts as King's Sarcophagus, so you effectively run 6. It adds a Horus monster from your deck to your hand (you put 1 card on the bottom of the deck) and draws 1 card whenever Horus the Black Flame Deity activates.

cards.name: Hapi, Guidance of Horus
cards.note: Horus monster that Special Summons itself from the Graveyard. When one of your cards is removed by the opponent it adds or shuffles back 2 cards from the Graveyard or banished pile. Part of the Selection Box.

substitutes.name: Qebehsenuef, Protection of Horus
substitutes.why: The creator says you can play without the Selection Box cards and put another Qebehsenuef or another Horus in their place. You still play, but the turn-one line he shows needs all four Horus monsters from the Graveyard, so it becomes weaker.

cards.name: Duamutef, Blessing of Horus
cards.note: Horus monster that Special Summons itself from the Graveyard. It gets 1200 ATK/DEF for each Horus monster you control, and when the opponent removes one of your cards you draw 1 card for each differently named monster in your Main Monster Zone.

cards.name: Qebehsenuef, Protection of Horus
cards.note: Horus monster that Special Summons itself from the Graveyard. When the opponent removes one of your cards it makes your Horus monsters untargetable by attacks and effects for the turn.

substitutes.name: Horus the Black Flame Deity
substitutes.why: The creator says a spare slot can hold another Horus monster. A second copy cannot be used if the first one is already on the field, but it is a good discard for King's Sarcophagus and Canopic Protector.

cards.name: Horus the Black Flame Deity
cards.note: The boss. It never comes back from the Graveyard, so keep it in your hand. With a Horus monster and King's Sarcophagus you reveal it to send a card from your hand or field and a card from the field to the Graveyard. If one of your Horus monsters or your King's Sarcophagus is removed by the opponent it Special Summons itself and can send every other monster to the Graveyard, yours included.

cards.name: Canopic Protector
cards.note: Continuous Trap and the best card to discard. Once per chain, when the opponent activates something, it Special Summons a Horus monster from your hand or Graveyard. When it is sent to the Graveyard it Sets itself again (banished when it leaves the field). Activate it first when you have several effects to chain.

cards.name: Soul Servant
cards.note: Quick-Play Spell that Dark Magician of Destruction searches. Discard it with King's Sarcophagus, then banish it from the Graveyard to draw 1 card for each differently named Dark Magician or Palladium monster on the field and in the Graveyards.

cards.name: D.D. Crow
cards.note: Free hand trap from the structure deck. It also counts as one of the 6 DARK monsters the skill needs.

substitutes.name: Witch of the Black Forest
substitutes.why: Some players use her as their Normal Summon to search Droll & Lock Bird or D.D. Crow (her search takes a monster with low DEF, and she is DARK too, so the skill still counts her). The creator tried the idea and did not find it interesting, because this deck already draws a lot of cards, so treat it as an option, not a recommendation.

cards.name: Droll & Lock Bird
cards.note: One of the best hand traps right now: it stops the opponent's search turn, and Horus draws a lot of cards. The creator says that if he owned 3 he would play 3, and that it is best when you go second.

substitutes.name: Effect Veiler
substitutes.why: The creator says you can put Effect Veiler or any hand traps you own in the free staple slots. Effect Veiler negates one monster effect instead of stopping searches.

cards.name: Mulcharmy Fuwalos
cards.note: Hand trap that draws a card each time the opponent Special Summons from the Deck or Extra Deck. It is one of the 6 WIND monsters that let you use the Wind version of the skill.

substitutes.name: Effect Veiler
substitutes.why: Effect Veiler is a free hand trap that stops one monster effect. The creator says to fill the staple slots with the hand traps you own.

substitutes.name: Powersink Stone
substitutes.why: The creator says there are safer, more stalling versions of the deck that put some traps in place of hand traps, for example this other Continuous Trap (it shuts down monster effects once 2 monster effects have been activated). Meta lists also run it.

cards.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
cards.note: Stops decks that make many Special Summons (including Horus itself): you will not lose to one interruption because Canopic Protector keeps bringing monsters back. If you brick too often, the creator says you can cut the Nibirus and the Droll & Lock Birds and play more engine cards, which makes the deck easier to play.

substitutes.name: Book of Moon
substitutes.why: The creator says the stall versions of the deck run Book of Moon and other traps instead of some hand traps. His own version keeps the hand traps because they work on turn one and turn two.

substitutes.name: Powersink Stone
substitutes.why: Same idea: a Continuous Trap in the stall version instead of a hand trap, which is safer when you go second.

cards.name: Lava Golem
cards.note: Kaiju-style card that removes two monsters from the opponent's field. You do not need your Normal Summon in this deck. The creator says Kaijus are needed because many cards are unaffected by everything else, and that you can also use the free one-tribute Kaijus from the tickets if you do not own Lava Golem.

cards.name: Dark Magician of Destruction
cards.note: Special Summon it by banishing Imsety (Level 8 DARK Spellcaster) in a turn you activated a Spell, then search Soul Servant. It also counts as a Dark Magician for Soul Servant's draw.

cards.name: Coach King Giantrainer
cards.note: Rank 8 Xyz made from 3 Level 8 monsters. Detach a material to draw a card and deal 400 damage if it is a monster. It is the first Xyz of turn one and fills your hand. You cannot attack the turn you use it.

cards.name: I:P Masquerena
cards.note: Link-2 made from Coach King plus a fourth monster. It makes your Link monsters safe from effect destruction and lets you Link Summon on the opponent's turn. The creator understands players who do not own it: the deck is still playable without it, only harder.

cards.name: S:P Little Knight
cards.note: Link-2 made on the opponent's turn with I:P Masquerena. If it uses an Extra Deck monster as material, it banishes a card on the field or in a Graveyard. It also banishes two face-up monsters in response to the opponent's effect.

substitutes.name: Knightmare Unicorn
substitutes.why: The creator says Knightmare Unicorn is fine if you do not own S:P Little Knight, but S:P is much stronger. Unicorn is a Link-3: you send 1 card from your hand to the Graveyard and return a card from the opponent's field to their deck.

cards.name: Underworld Goddess of the Closed World
cards.note: Link-5 made with the opponent's monster as one material. It negates the effects of the opponent's face-up monsters and negates a Special Summon from the Graveyard once per turn.

cards.name: Knightmare Phoenix
cards.note: Link-2 that discards a card to destroy a Spell or Trap, a good answer now that Sarcophagus decks are popular. The creator hesitated between this and Number 38.

substitutes.name: Number 38: Hope Harbinger Dragon Titanic Galaxy
substitutes.why: The creator says it is a matter of preference. Number 38 is a Rank 8 that negates and steals a Spell the opponent activates, so it is more passive.

cards.name: Dingirsu, the Orcust of the Evening Star

mathmech.gamePlan: Open with a Level 4 Mathmech Tuner (a small monster that lets you Synchro Summon) and use the skill to put the key monsters in your hand. Chain extra summons (an extender is a card that lets you summon more monsters) into Xyz and Link monsters (Xyz and Link are special monsters that live in the Extra Deck) that search, remove the opponent's cards, and draw. Finish with Geomathmech Final Sigma, a Level 12 monster that hits for double damage. When you search with the skill, take Circular and Diameter first, then Sigma, then Addition and Subtraction: keeping Sigma in your hand is safer than leaving it in the Graveyard, because a hand trap (a card the opponent plays from their hand) can stop it coming back, and Addition and Subtraction summon themselves from your hand, so they keep your follow-up going if you get interrupted. Because the skill gets you to your combo pieces, the rest of your deck goes to tech cards: hand traps and board breakers (cards that clear the opponent's board). Always check this guide's sources: the creators disagree on small details, and both mention a banlist change was coming when they recorded.
strengths: Out-resources opponents: the skill keeps adding monsters every turn, so you do not run out of cards early.
Several searches and a draw happen before the opponent can respond, which dodges some hand traps.
From turn 2 you can set a Mathmech trap and end the duel with Geomathmech Final Sigma.
weaknesses: Hand traps still hurt: D.D. Crow on the targets of Splash Mage's revive is very bad, and you are only protected against Effect Veiler and Infinite Impermanence for a short part of the combo.
In a long game the top decks (Vaalmonica, Branded, Snake-Eye) generate more resources than you do.
The deck leans heavily on tech cards, so a bad draw of tech cards makes it much weaker.
The Portuguese creator (Ignister) advises against building it right now because a banlist change and new decks were expected; check the current list before you spend gems.

memento.gamePlan: Memento is a combo deck: almost every card destroys or sends another, and each destruction triggers more effects. The goal is a field that is hard to break and a Mementoal Tecuhtlica - Combined Creation (5000 ATK) that you can bring back every turn. Start with a starter (Mementotlan Angwitch, Mementotlan Dark Blade or Mementotlan Tatsunootoshigo), use Mementotlan Fusion to make Mementomictlan Tecuhtlica - Creation King, destroy it for its effects, and finish with Combined Creation, Lyrilusc - Assembled Nightingale (a protective Xyz monster) and I:P Masquerena (a Link monster that turns into your negate on the opponent's turn). The creator says the deck has many lines and this video shows only the simplest; learn this one first, then add others from other creators. Do not pick up the deck and expect to master it quickly: the creator practised for more than 4 hours and still did not learn every play.
strengths: It fills your hand and Graveyard so fast that you can have 10 cards in hand by the end of the combo.
Almost everything protects itself: monsters come back from the Graveyard, and Lyrilusc - Assembled Nightingale makes sure you cannot lose the first turn.
On the opponent's turn you have several answers at once: Forbidden Droplet, Fracture Dance, Cranium Burst and I:P Masquerena into S:P Little Knight.
The creator says it has an answer to every kind of play and a clear way to win with Combined Creation attacking directly.
weaknesses: It is complex: you can lose games by playing the combo wrong or by running out of time while you learn.
D.D. Crow on Mementotlan Ghattic (or Bystial on a LIGHT or DARK Memento) ruins the main line, and Combined Creation is best protected in hand.

Combined Creation can be hit by a negate, a Dark Ruler No More or a banish; the creator says the only monster effect that matters to negate on his turn is Mementotlan Tatsunootoshigo, Dark Blade or Angwitch.
The deck leans on tech cards (hand traps, selection-box cards) that depend on what you own.

scenarios.title: Turn 1 with Tatsunootoshigo in your hand: build Combined Creation and a protected field

skillPlan.note: The skill is step 1: it replaces a card from your hand with 2 new cards. In the replay he put Bone Party back.

start.note: The creator's opening hand (Tatsunootoshigo, Cranium Burst, Shleepy and Bone Party). Yours will differ: the same line works with other cards, and with Angwitch or Dark Blade you search or replace Tatsunootoshigo instead.

steps.when: Right at the start of your Main Phase
steps.needs: Any 1 card from your hand to put on the bottom of your deck (or send to the Graveyard). The creator returns Mementotlan Bone Party, because he can fetch it back later.
steps.gives: You draw 2 cards (3 if you are the second player on the first turn). Here you draw Mementotlan Goblin and Mementotlan Fracture Dance.
steps.reason: The skill turns a clumsy card into 2 new ones. The creator says that in this deck sending cards to the Graveyard is good too, and that it is best to send back a duplicate Level 1 or Level 3 monster.
Special Summon Mementotlan Tatsunootoshigo from your hand. You can do this when you control no face-up monsters except Memento monsters, so do it before anything else is on your side of the field.

Destroy Tatsunootoshigo itself, then send Memento monsters with different names from your deck to the Graveyard, with Levels adding up to at most its own Level 5. In this line always send Mementotlan Ghattic (Level 2) and Mementotlan Shleepy (Level 3). Destroying a Memento monster this turn is what lets Shleepy come out later.
Ghattic was sent to the Graveyard by a Memento monster's effect, so it Special Summons itself. Then its effect adds a Memento card from your Graveyard to your hand: take Shleepy back.

A Memento monster was destroyed this turn, so Shleepy can Special Summon itself from your hand. When it is summoned it Fusion Summons a Memento Fusion monster using monsters from your hand or field: Mementotlan Twin Dragon, with Shleepy and Ghattic as the materials.

Because it was Fusion Summoned, Twin Dragon destroys itself and adds up to 2 Memento monsters with different names from your deck to your hand: Mementoal Tecuhtlica - Combined Creation (your boss monster, kept in hand where a Dark Ruler No More or a hand trap cannot hit it) and Mementotlan Dark Blade.
Twin Dragon was destroyed, so it Special Summons a Level 6 or lower Memento monster from the Graveyard: Ghattic comes back.
Normal Summon Mementotlan Dark Blade. This is your only Normal Summon of the turn, so you cannot also search it with Tatsunootoshigo if you want it in hand later.
Dark Blade destroys a Memento monster you control (Ghattic) to Special Summon a Level 3 or lower Memento monster from your deck: Mementotlan Mace.
Mace destroys a Memento monster you control (Dark Blade) and adds any Memento card from your deck to your hand: take Mementotlan Fusion. If you already hold Fusion, search something else here.

Activate Mementotlan Fusion: Fusion Summon Mementomictlan Tecuhtlica - Creation King (Level 9) using Mementotlan Goblin from your hand and, because a Memento monster was destroyed this turn, Twin Dragon and Dark Blade from your Graveyard as extra materials (they go back to the Extra Deck and the deck).

Because Creation King was Fusion Summoned it sends 3 Memento cards from your deck or Extra Deck to the Graveyard: Mementotlan Dark Blade, Mementotlan Angwitch and Mementotlan Akihiron. These are all monsters you want in the Graveyard for later.

Banish Mementotlan Fusion from your Graveyard to destroy Creation King (a Memento monster you control), and add a Memento Spell/Trap to your hand: Mementotlan Bone Party. In the creator's words, the destroyed Creation King has already done its work and the destruction triggers more effects below.

A Memento monster you controlled was destroyed, so Mementotlan Akihiron Special Summons itself from the Graveyard. While it is on the field your Level 9 or higher Memento monsters can attack directly (the key to this deck's one-turn kills).
Banish Creation King from the Graveyard to add the Field Spell Mementomictlan to your hand. Because it waits in the Graveyard you do not need to rush to search the field.

Activate the Field Spell Mementomictlan. Your Memento monsters are protected from trap responses in battle, destroyed ones can come back, and each end phase it sets a Memento Spell/Trap from the Graveyard.

Activate Mementotlan Bone Party: destroy Akihiron and Special Summon a Memento monster with another name from your deck in Defense Position: Mementotlan Angwitch. Every destruction now sets off more effects.

Three effects trigger at once, so line them up as one chain: Angwitch adds a Memento monster from your deck (take Mementotlan-Horned Dragon); Akihiron adds a banished Memento card to your hand (take Mementotlan Fusion back); and the Field Spell Special Summons Mementotlan Goblin from the Graveyard to replace the destroyed Akihiron.

Goblin and Mace are two Level 1 monsters, so Xyz Summon Lyrilusc - Assembled Nightingale (Rank 1). On the opponent's draw you can detach a material to protect your Lyrilusc monsters, and you take no battle damage that turn. This is the creator's insurance against a bad turn.

You now have 3 or more Memento monsters with different names in the Graveyard, so Mementotlan-Horned Dragon Special Summons itself from your hand. Its destruction would also take down 2 of the opponent's cards.

Link Summon I:P Masquerena using Angwitch and Horned Dragon. On the opponent's turn you can use it to Link Summon S:P Little Knight (or a Knightmare Unicorn or Underworld Goddess of the Closed World) and remove a card.

Special Summon Mementoal Tecuhtlica - Combined Creation (Level 11, 5000 ATK) by shuffling 5 Memento monsters with different names from your hand and Graveyard into the deck: Horned Dragon, Dark Blade, Angwitch, Tatsunootoshigo and Shleepy. With Akihiron gone you can no longer attack directly this turn, but you are building the opponent's-turn defence.

Set Cranium Burst, Fracture Dance and Mementotlan Fusion (your hand still holds one card). Combined Creation lets Cranium Burst negate monster effects 5 times by lowering its ATK, Fracture Dance destroys 2 cards, and Fusion can answer the opponent's turn. If you hold Forbidden Droplet, keep it in hand instead of setting Fusion.

scenarios.chainNotes: Keep Forbidden Droplet in hand if you have it and set the remaining Spell/Trap cards. Do not summon Combined Creation if it is in your hand together with Creation King and you have fewer than 3 different Memento monsters in the Graveyard. Mementotlan Shleepy and Mementotlan Ghattic are the cards you want to be hit by the opponent least, so the creator advises adapting if D.D. Crow lands on Ghattic.
scenarios.endBoard: Mementoal Tecuhtlica - Combined Creation (5000 ATK) and Lyrilusc - Assembled Nightingale on the field with I:P Masquerena in the Extra Monster Zone, Mementomictlan active and Cranium Burst, Fracture Dance and Mementotlan Fusion set. One Shleepy stays in your hand.
scenarios.weakSpots: D.D. Crow on Mementotlan Ghattic breaks this line (you must find another route); a negate on the Fusion Summons or on Combined Creation's Special Summon slows you; and Combined Creation is not worth negating on the opponent's turn because its effect only revives a Memento, which is why the creator says to negate his starters instead.

scenarios.title: Turn 1 with Angwitch (and no Tatsunootoshigo): fetch it, and keep going when D.D. Crow banishes Ghattic

without.label: Tatsunootoshigo in your hand (use the first line instead)

skillPlan.note: The skill is step 1: it replaces a card in your hand with 2 new cards, here a second Angwitch and Shleepy.

start.note: The creator's opening hand (Fusion, Angwitch, Bone Party and Horned Dragon). Yours will differ: any hand with Angwitch can start this way. Putting Bone Party back is his choice, because he can fetch it again later.

steps.when: Right at the start of your Main Phase
steps.needs: Any 1 card from your hand to put on the bottom of your deck. The creator returns Mementotlan Bone Party.
steps.gives: You draw 2 cards (here Mementotlan Shleepy and a second Mementotlan Angwitch).
steps.reason: The creator did not have Tatsunootoshigo in this hand, so the skill is used to look for another way into the combo: here it gives a second Angwitch.

Normal Summon Mementotlan Angwitch and use its effect to add a Memento monster from your deck to your hand: take Mementotlan Tatsunootoshigo, your best starter. This is how you start the combo when you did not open with it.
Special Summon Mementotlan Tatsunootoshigo from your hand (you control no face-up monsters except Memento monsters).
Destroy Tatsunootoshigo itself and send Mementotlan Ghattic and Mementotlan Shleepy from your deck to the Graveyard (Levels 2 and 3 add up to its Level 5).

Ghattic was sent by a Memento effect, so it tries to Special Summon itself. In this replay the opponent answers with D.D. Crow, which banishes Ghattic from the Graveyard. This is the deck's worst answer, and the creator says you must be ready to continue without Ghattic.

With Ghattic gone, use Mementotlan Fusion right away: Fusion Summon Mementotlan Twin Dragon with a second Mementotlan Angwitch from your hand and Mementotlan Tatsunootoshigo from your Graveyard (shuffled back into the deck, because a Memento monster was destroyed this turn).
Twin Dragon destroys itself and adds up to 2 Memento monsters with different names from your deck to your hand: Mementoal Tecuhtlica - Combined Creation and Mementotlan Tatsunootoshigo again.
Because Twin Dragon was destroyed, Special Summon a Level 6 or lower Memento monster from the Graveyard. Ghattic is banished, so take Mementotlan Shleepy.

Shleepy Fusion Summons Mementomictlan Tecuhtlica - Creation King using itself from the field plus Mementotlan Tatsunootoshigo and Combined Creation from your hand. Putting Combined Creation in the Graveyard is deliberate: it Special Summons itself from there at the end of the turn.

Creation King sends 3 Memento cards from your deck to the Graveyard: Mementotlan Fracture Dance, Mementotlan Mace and Mementotlan Akihiron. Fracture Dance is sent on purpose: the Field Spell sets it again at the end of the turn.
Angwitch destroys itself to Special Summon a Level 2 or lower Memento monster from the Graveyard: Mementotlan Mace (the one Creation King just sent).
Angwitch was destroyed, so Mementotlan Akihiron Special Summons itself from the Graveyard.
Mace destroys Creation King (a Memento monster you control) and adds a Memento card from your deck to your hand: take Mementotlan Goblin.
Banish Creation King from the Graveyard to add the Field Spell Mementomictlan to your hand, then activate it.
Banish Mementotlan Fusion from the Graveyard to destroy Akihiron and add a Memento Spell/Trap to your hand: Mementotlan Bone Party.

Two effects trigger because Akihiron was destroyed: Akihiron adds Mementotlan Fusion back from the banished zone, and the Field Spell Special Summons Mementotlan Angwitch from the Graveyard to replace it. Angwitch cannot search again, because it already did this turn.

Activate Mementotlan Bone Party: destroy Angwitch and Special Summon Mementotlan Dark Blade from your deck in Defense Position. Mementotlan-Horned Dragon can then Special Summon itself from your hand, because 3 Memento monsters with different names are in the Graveyard.
Link Summon I:P Masquerena using Dark Blade and Horned Dragon. It will turn into your negate on the opponent's turn.

Special Summon Mementoal Tecuhtlica - Combined Creation from your Graveyard by shuffling 5 Memento monsters with different names back: Horned Dragon, Twin Dragon (back to the Extra Deck), Tatsunootoshigo, Angwitch and Dark Blade.

Set Mementotlan Fusion. At the end of the turn the Field Spell also sets Mementotlan Fracture Dance from the Graveyard for you, so you end with 2 Traps/Quick-Play cards ready for the opponent's turn. Keep Mementotlan Goblin in hand: with Combined Creation on the field it can discard itself to stop the opponent from targeting your Memento monsters.

scenarios.chainNotes: In this replay the opponent plays D.D. Crow on Ghattic. If it happens, do not stop: the creator uses Mementotlan Fusion at once and relies on Twin Dragon and Shleepy, which do not need Ghattic. Keep Combined Creation in the Graveyard until the last step, where it Special Summons itself.
scenarios.endBoard: Combined Creation and Mementotlan Mace on the field with I:P Masquerena in the Extra Monster Zone, Mementomictlan active and Mementotlan Fusion and Mementotlan Fracture Dance set. Shleepy and Goblin stay in your hand.
scenarios.weakSpots: D.D. Crow on Ghattic makes this line one step longer but the creator still finishes it; a hand trap on Angwitch's search or on the first Fusion stops it earlier, so the creator keeps Tatsunootoshigo as the preferred start.
